title: Summoned to another State: must you go?

scenes.dialogue: You run a business in Karnataka. Police from another State send you a notice to come to their police station, in their State. Are you bound to go?
Here, Maharashtra police came to Tumkur, took statements and business records, and never told the Karnataka police. So was any of it lawful?
Hi, I'm Ravishankar from LawWorld. On twenty ninth October, twenty twenty six, Honourable Justice Suraj Govindaraj of the Karnataka High Court ruled.

scenes.dialogue: On nineteenth August, twenty twenty five, Maharashtra police stopped a truck near Kolhapur. Next day, a food safety case was filed against unknown persons.

scenes.dialogue: Yet their statements were recorded right there in Tumkur. The traders argued Section One Seventy Nine reaches only people within that station or an adjoining one.

scenes.dialogue: Finally, what did the High Court decide? The notices could not make traders in Tumkur appear at Vadgaon, and the visit, without telling local police, was unlawful.
So its statements can't be relied on, and ledgers held unlawfully must go back. Next time, Vadgaon must first inform Karnataka police in writing. The F I R stays.
